reason: Tricostate means three-ribbed: a count of ribs (costae), like '5-nerved'. The same scale has 'ecostate' at the other end, so this is a count of parts and not a new value.

A compound of two existing values: ovate (PATO_0001891, synonym ovoid) and elliptic (PATO_0000947, synonym ellipsoid), with the modifier 'broadly'. It is read as a continuum between them, like 'linear-lanceolate'.
A fern lamina apex 'pinna-like' resembles the lateral pinnae (leaflet PO_0020049). That is a resemblance to another part, not a shape of its own.
Bark or periderm flaking off is exfoliating, which already has 'flaking' as a synonym.

The word is a part noun with mixed meanings: pellucid gland dots on leaves, but colour spots on the corolla. It is meaningless without its qualifier; 'gland-dotted' (FLOPO:0991174) and 'spotted' already cover the clear cases.
Says outright that lenticels are present; same rule as 'lenticellate'.
Bark or branches cracked lengthwise are fissured, which has 'cracked' as a related synonym. The 'on drying' bud example is a specimen condition (pattern 06).
The symmetry belongs to the set of stamens, tepals or nerves, not to each member, so it is symmetrical (PATO_0000632) of the whole. 'More symmetrically' is a comparison and is out of scope.

In 'dried leaves present at anthesis' and 'there persist 5 dried sepals', the parts have withered on the living plant without being shed, which is marcescent. 'When dry' as a herbarium condition stays with pattern 06.
A part, not a quality; the PO class exists.
Catenate hairs are made of a chain of cells constricted at the cross-walls, like a string of beads. That is moniliform.
These are bacterial leaf nodules (as in Rubiaceae). PO has only root nodules (PO_0003023), so there is no part to state the absence of; a leaf-nodule bearer class is needed first.
Hairs with swollen glandular bases make the surface pustulate, whose definition names elevations at the bases of hairs. The alternative would be a new hair-type class.

reason: Two qualities that hold together, not a continuum: the part is linear and ends in an awn (same rule as 'aristate'). It splits into two annotations.

reason: Combines stellate hairs with a slightly rough surface (scabrous, which has 'scaberulous' as a synonym). These are two values, not one new quality.
Half-spreading, at about 45 degrees between erect and patent: directed upward at an oblique angle, which is ascending.
'Ventrally dihedral' seeds have two flat faces meeting at an angle on the ventral side. That is an angular region, not a new shape.
Ovoid (ovate, PATO_0001891) qualified as not exactly so. 'Irregularly' weakens an existing value rather than naming a new one.
Mirrors the earlier rule 'enlarged' = increased size. Where the comparison is 'towards the base', it reads as a position (pattern 18).
A spadix without a sterile appendix is not appendiculate. PO has no spadix-appendix part to state the absence of.
Achenes and seeds with a distinct marginal band are margined; 'broadly' is a degree of that band, as 'narrowly margined' is.
Covered with gland-like warts. The quality is the warty surface, as with the earlier 'verrucose' rule; the glandular nature is detail of the warts.
The veins are present (as in the rule for 'nerved') but hard to see. The quality inheres in the veins (vascular bundle PO_0005020) of the sepal or bract.
'Evident' is conspicuous (earlier rule C323); 'faintly evident' veins are barely visible, i.e. inconspicuous.
Fuchsia is a vivid purplish red, a colour made of red and blue hues: magenta.
The orchid flower is not turned upside down; this is the negation of the existing resupinate.
Ivory here is a creamy white colour. PATO 'ivory' (PATO_0002149) means radiopacity in X-rays and must not be used.
Rotting cataphylls and rootstocks 'without form' lack a distinct morphology, which is amorphous.
Latin castaneus means chestnut-brown.
Amplectent means embracing or clasping the axis, like amplexicaul, which was already replaced by PATO clasping.
